subject: MAP: cost discrepancy — runbook to reconcile tokens/$ and caching assumptions
messages:
From: Lara Quinn <lara@acmehealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-03-10T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: MAP: early numbers look worse than expected

Hi Grace / Jordan,

Quick one — finance ran the MAP economics with our expected traffic shape and the numbers came back ~40% worse on tokens/$ than the draft you provided. The main drivers our team flagged: average request length is higher than the MAP baseline (we're seeing 550-700 tokens median per request versus the MAP assumption of ~220), and the prefix cache hit rate is much lower in our snapshot (about 25% versus your 45% assumption).

Attached is the spreadsheet they sent (summary tab). Can you confirm whether the MAP used the same traffic mix and if there were any additional caching or batching optimizations assumed?

We want to avoid last-minute budget surprises before approval. Would like a concrete mitigation plan and the smallest set of experiments we can run to reconcile.

Thanks,
Lara Quinn
Head of Product Ops
Acme Health

Attachments: acme_finance_sample_export.csv (CSV summary)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Lara Quinn <lara@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-03-10T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: early numbers look worse than expected

Lara — thanks for the heads up and for sharing the finance export. We dug in and reproduced the delta locally; good catch. Short summary of findings and an action runbook below. We can walk through this in 30 minutes if helpful.

Summary (what happened)
- MAP baseline (what we originally shared): 350k tokens/$ (baseline mix: 60% short Q&A <= 200 tokens, 30% medium 200-600 tokens, 10% long >600 tokens). Expected prefix cache hit = 45%.
- Acme snapshot (finance export): effective ~210k tokens/$ (≈40% worse), median request ~580 tokens, prefix cache hit ≈25%.
- Drivers: heavier long-request tail, lower cacheable prefix fraction, and lower batching utilization in their current client (no continuous batching + short inter-arrival times).

Runbook (concrete steps and owners) — "Cost Reconciliation Runbook"
1) Traffic alignment (Grace / Acme): Lara to confirm a 48-hour production-ish sample (anonymized) or the proxy traces. If not possible, share a representative CSV of request lengths + timestamps. Goal: produce a traffic mix CSV we can simulate. (Due: 2029-03-11 12:00 PT)
2) Simulation re-run (Karthik): Rerun cost sims using Acme traffic mix with three configs:
   a) MAP baseline (prefetch caching + batching enabled)
   b) MAP baseline + aggressive prefix caching (pre-warm top 5% prefixes)
   c) Realistic client (no continuous batching) + our autoscaling policy
   Deliverable: per-config tokens/$, per-seq latency tail, and cache-hit sensitivity. Include a delta column vs MAP baseline. (Due: 2029-03-11 18:00 PT)
3) Pilot canary (Jordan / Neha): If sims show >20% variance still, spin a 3-day pilot (100k queries/day) against Dedicated burst pool to measure real tokens/$ with real client behavior. Pilot config will include: prefix caching ON, batching window 30ms, kv-cache TTL 24h, sampling logs for token counts. Draft SLA and pilot plan attached. (Target start: 2029-03-15)
4) Quick client fixes (Acme): Small SDK change to enable client-side batching and an optional prefix-hash header for caching. Neha to provide a one-file SDK patch for a quick rollback. (Neha due: 2029-03-12)
5) Decision gates (Grace):
   - If pilot tokens/$ within 15% of MAP baseline => proceed to close and include caching onboarding in SOW.
   - If pilot tokens/$ worse by >15% => finance to reconvene and consider price-adjusted pilot or committed capacity.

Numbers to watch (start points)
- MAP baseline: 350000 tokens per $ (baseline)
- Acme snapshot: 210000 tokens per $ (observed)
- Cache hit delta needed: moving hit rate from 25% -> 45% reduces effective tokens consumed by ~18-22% in our sims (depends on long-tail length).

Attachments: acme_simulation_spreadsheet_v2.csv (we'll drop our simulation sheets in the shared Drive), pilot_sla_draft.pdf.

Next steps: Lara — can you confirm whether you can share sampled traces or we should work off the CSV they already sent? Jordan / Karthik / Neha, I'll mark action items in the HubSpot deal after you ack.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
